newsitem.title: USA: Time Warner, Turner chiefs to meet - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Time Warner, Turner chiefs to meet - WSJ.

text.p: Time Warner Inc chairman Gerald Levin and Turner Broadcasting System Inc chairman Ted Turner will meet at Turner's Montana ranch to hammer out contentious issues as they prepare to combine the two media giants, The Wall Street Journal reported on Friday.

One top item for Turner at Friday's meeting is expected to be the fate of Turner's New Line Cinema. Turner is said to be annoyed that Time Warner openly floated a plan to sell the motion-picture studio after the merger closes.
People who have talked to Turner about New Line say he believes Time Warner should keep the studio and is expected to press the issue at Friday's meeting.

The two companies are trying to resolve issues so they can issue proxy statements. The $6.5 billion merger is still awaiting approval from the federal government and is expected to close in mid-October.

Levin and Turner also are expected to debate which divisions should bear the brunt of expected layoffs. Last week, Turner told executives that the combined company may have to cut up to 1,000 jobs and $100 million in expenses after the merger.
